per_case_results.query: How is the value of interest-free or concessional loan provided by employer for education/medical purposes calculated for a salaried employee under Rule 15 (2026 rules)?
per_case_results.direct_answer: Under Rule 15 (sub-rule 5 / Table IV) of the Income-tax Rules, 2026, the perquisite value of an interest-free or concessional loan provided by an employer is calculated by applying the annual interest rate charged by the State Bank of India (SBI) as on the 1st day of the relevant tax year (for the same purpose) to the maximum outstanding monthly balance, minus any interest actually paid by the employee. For medical loans, no perquisite value is charged if the loan is for specified diseases under Rule 18 (unless reimbursed by insurance) or if total aggregate loans do not exceed Rs. 2,00,000. Educational loans follow the standard SBI interest calculation unless the total aggregate loan threshold of Rs. 2,00,000 applies.
per_case_results.temporal_applicability: Applies under the Income-tax Rules, 2026 for the tax year (Financial Year) relevant to Assessment Year 2026-27 onwards.

per_case_results.query: I am a senior citizen aged 77 who receives only pension and interest income. Can I submit a declaration to my bank under Rule 26D so that no tax return is required to be filed?
per_case_results.direct_answer: Yes, as a senior citizen aged 75 years or above receiving only pension and interest income (from the same specified bank), you can submit a paper declaration in Form No. 12BBA to your specified bank under Rule 26D of the Income-tax Rules, 1962. Upon submitting this declaration along with evidence of Chapter VI-A deductions, the specified bank will compute your total income, apply applicable deductions and section 87A rebates, and deduct the appropriate tax. Consequently, you will be exempted from filing an income tax return under section 194P.
per_case_results.temporal_applicability: Rule 26D came into effect on 2-9-2021 and is applicable from Assessment Year (AY) 2022-23 (Financial Year 2021-22) onwards.

citations.citation_text: The declaration required to be furnished by the specified senior citizen to the specified bank under sub-clause (iii) of clause (b) of Explanation to section 194P shall be in Form No. 12BBA to be furnished in paper form duly verified.

On furnishing of the declaration in Form No. 12BBA, the specified bank shall, after giving effect to the deduction allowable under Chapter VI-A and rebate allowable under section 87A, compute the total income of such specified senior citizen for the relevant assessment year and deduct income-tax on such total income on the basis of the rates in force.

per_case_results.query: How is the value of interest-free or concessional loan provided by employer for education/medical purposes calculated for a salaried employee under Rule 3 (1962 rules)?
How is the value of interest-free or concessional loan provided by employer for education/medical purposes calculated for a salaried employee under Rule 3 (1962 rules)?
per_case_results.direct_answer: Under Rule 3(7) of the Income-tax Rules, 1962, the perquisite value of an interest-free or concessional loan provided by an employer is calculated by applying the interest rate charged by the State Bank of India (SBI) as on the 1st day of the relevant previous year (for the same purpose) to the maximum outstanding monthly balance, reduced by any interest actually paid by the employee or their household member. For medical loans taken for diseases specified in Rule 3A, the perquisite value is nil (exempt), except to the extent the medical expenses are reimbursed under a medical insurance scheme. Loans for education purposes follow the standard SBI benchmark interest calculation without a specific exemption unless the aggregate petty loan threshold (not exceeding ₹20,000) applies.
per_case_results.temporal_applicability: Applicable under Rule 3(7) of the Income-tax Rules, 1962 (effective from 01-09-2023). In Indian taxation, the perquisite is computed for the relevant Previous Year (Financial Year - FY) and assessed in the immediately following Assessment Year (AY).

citations.citation_text: The value of the benefit to the assessee resulting from the provision of interest-free or concessional loan for any purpose... shall be determined as the sum equal to the interest computed at the rate charged per annum by the State Bank of India... as on the 1st day of the relevant previous year in respect of loans for the same purpose advanced by it on the maximum outstanding monthly balance as reduced by the interest, if any, actually paid... Provided that no value would be charged if such loans are made available for medical treatment in respect of diseases specified in rule 3A... or where the amount of loans are petty not exceeding in the aggregate twenty thousand rupees: Provided further that... the exemption so provided shall not apply to so much of the loan as has been reimbursed to the employee under any medical insurance scheme.

Mentions Rs. 20,000 threshold or medical treatment exemption
